skill.name: graphite-cli
skill.description: Provides practical guidance for creating, managing, submitting, synchronizing, and restructuring stacked pull requests with the Graphite CLI.
skill.summary: Guide Graphite CLI workflows for stacked branches and pull requests.
skill.author: Calel33

security_audit.summary: All 43 external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around documented Graphite and Git terms; the skill contains no executable script. The network-reconnaissance finding is false because the cited line documents submitting branches to GitHub. No prompt injection, credential collection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

content.user_title: Master Graphite CLI Stacked Pull Request Workflows
content.value_statement: Stacked pull requests are difficult to create, reorder, synchronize, and submit with confidence. This skill provides Graphite CLI guidance from setup through collaboration.
actual_capabilities: Explains Graphite authentication, repository initialization, and trunk selection.
Guides branch creation, commit updates, draft submission, and full-stack submission.
Maps common Graphite commands to aliases and expected effects.
Covers stack visualization, branch navigation, synchronization, and conflict continuation.
Explains stack restructuring with move, fold, split, insert, and absorb operations.
Describes shared-stack workflows, branch tracking, freezing, merging, and cleanup.
limitations: Provides documentation and guidance but does not install Graphite or execute commands.
Cannot inspect repository state, verify branch relationships, or resolve merge conflicts automatically.
Some commands amend, rebase, delete, or force-push branches and require careful review.
Bundled command details may differ from the latest Graphite CLI release.

use_cases.title: Create a first stacked pull request
use_cases.description: Learn the setup, branch creation, and submission sequence for a small dependent change.

use_cases.title: Update a stack after review
use_cases.description: Apply feedback, amend the correct branch, restack dependent work, and resubmit pull requests.

use_cases.title: Restructure a complex branch stack
use_cases.description: Choose commands for moving, folding, splitting, inserting, or absorbing changes across dependent branches.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Graphite
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to authenticate Graphite and initialize my Git repository with main as the trunk branch.

prompt_templates.title: Create and submit a stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Graphite commands for three dependent changes, with each pull request submitted as a draft.

prompt_templates.title: Handle review changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the workflow for updating the middle branch of my stack, resolving conflicts, and resubmitting every affected pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign a stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare move, fold, split, insert, and absorb for reorganizing my stack, then recommend a sequence based on my branch relationships.

output_examples.input: How do I start using Graphite in an existing repository?
output_examples.output: The response explains authentication, repository initialization, trunk selection, and verification before creating the first branch.

output_examples.input: I changed the second branch in a three-branch stack. What comes next?
output_examples.output: The response outlines amending the current branch, restacking dependents, checking conflicts, and updating the remote pull requests.

output_examples.input: Should I fold, move, or split this branch?
output_examples.output: The response compares each operation by goal, history impact, branch deletion behavior, and effect on dependent branches.

best_practices: Inspect the current branch and stack structure before running history-changing commands.
Keep each branch focused on one reviewable change and submit dependent branches in order.
Synchronize with trunk regularly and resolve conflicts before modifying stack structure.
anti_patterns: Do not force-push or fold branches without confirming the affected remote work.
Do not run broad staging commands when unrelated working-tree changes are present.
Do not reorder dependencies without first reviewing the complete branch stack.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Graphite commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance and workflow explanations for you or an authorized agent to follow.

faq.question: Do I need a Graphite account?
faq.answer: Graphite authentication is required for workflows that create or update pull requests on GitHub.

faq.question: Can I use the guidance with plain Git?
faq.answer: The concepts involve Git, but the documented commands assume that the Graphite CLI is installed and initialized.

faq.question: Can it help with merge conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the standard resolve, stage, and continue workflow, but it cannot resolve file contents automatically.

faq.question: Are the commands guaranteed to match the latest release?
faq.answer: No. Verify version-sensitive flags and installation steps against the current official Graphite documentation.

faq.question: Which commands require extra caution?
faq.answer: Submission, synchronization, modification, move, fold, split, and absorb operations can change local or remote history.
